title: Oscillations
subject: Physics
subtitle: Class 12 HSC & MHT-CET • Rapid Revision Deck

cards.q: Definition and differential equation of Linear Simple Harmonic Motion (SHM)?
cards.a:
SHM: Motion where restoring force is directly proportional to displacement from mean position and directed towards mean position (F = - k x).
Differential equation: d²x / dt² + ω² x = 0, where ω = √(k / m).
cards.hint: Acceleration is a = - ω² x. Negative sign confirms restoring nature directed towards center.

cards.q: Velocity of a particle performing SHM at displacement x?
cards.a:
v = ± ω √(A² - x²).
At mean position (x = 0): v_max = ω A.
At extreme positions (x = ± A): v = 0.
cards.hint: v-x graph of SHM is an ELLIPSE: x²/A² + v²/(ω²A²) = 1.

cards.q: Acceleration of a particle performing SHM at displacement x?
cards.a:
a = - ω² x.
At mean position (x = 0): a = 0.
At extreme positions (x = ± A): a_max = ω² A (directed toward mean position).
cards.hint: a-x graph is a straight line passing through origin with negative slope -ω².

cards.q: Displacement x(t) starting from Mean Position vs Extreme Position?
cards.a:
Starting from Mean Position (phase α = 0): x(t) = A sin(ω t).
Starting from Positive Extreme (phase α = π/2): x(t) = A cos(ω t).
cards.hint: General form: x(t) = A sin(ω t + α), where α is the epoch (initial phase).

cards.q: Phase differences between Displacement, Velocity, and Acceleration in SHM?
cards.a:
Displacement and Velocity: Phase difference is π/2 rad (90°, Velocity LEADS displacement).
Velocity and Acceleration: Phase difference is π/2 rad (90°, Acceleration LEADS velocity).
Displacement and Acceleration: Phase difference is π rad (180°, exact OPPOSITE phases).
cards.hint: Classic HSC theory 2-mark question! Acceleration and displacement are always in opposite phase.

cards.q: Kinetic Energy (K), Potential Energy (U), and Total Energy (E) in SHM?
cards.a:
K = (1/2) m ω² (A² - x²) = (1/2) k (A² - x²)
U = (1/2) m ω² x² = (1/2) k x²
Total Energy: E = K + U = (1/2) k A² = (1/2) m ω² A² = 2 π² m n² A².
cards.hint: Total energy E is strictly CONSTANT at all positions and at all times (E ∝ m, E ∝ n², E ∝ A²).

cards.q: At what displacements x is (1) K = U, and (2) K = 3 U in SHM?
cards.hint: Top MHT-CET high-frequency question! At x = A/2, 75% energy is kinetic and 25% is potential.

cards.q: Average Kinetic Energy and Average Potential Energy over one complete cycle in SHM?
cards.a:
Time average: <K>_time = (1/4) k A² = E / 2
<U>_time = (1/4) k A² = E / 2.
Position average: <K>_pos = (2/3) E; <U>_pos = (1/3) E.
cards.hint: Over a full time period, average KE equals average PE, each exactly half the total energy (E/2).

cards.q: Time period of a Simple Pendulum of length L?
cards.a: T = 2π √(L / g) ⇒ frequency n = (1 / 2π) √(g / L).
cards.hint: Valid for small angular amplitudes (θ < 10°) where sin θ ≈ θ.

cards.q: Laws of Simple Pendulum?
cards.a:
1. Law of Length: T ∝ √L (at constant g).
2. Law of Gravity: T ∝ 1 / √g (at constant L).
3. Law of Mass: T is independent of bob mass.
4. Law of Isochronism: T is independent of amplitude (for small oscillations).
cards.hint: Replacing a hollow bob with a solid lead bob of same size does NOT change time period.

cards.q: What is a Seconds Pendulum and what is its length on Earth (g = 9.8 m/s²)?
cards.a:
A pendulum whose time period is exactly 2 seconds (T = 2 s, so one tick or half-vibration is 1 s).
Length: L = g / π² ≈ 9.8 / (3.1416)² ≈ 0.993 m ≈ 100 cm (1 metre).
cards.hint: Remember: T = 2 s, NOT 1 s! Length is very close to 1 metre.

cards.q: Spring Combinations: Effective spring constant and time period for Series vs Parallel?
cards.a:
Series: 1 / k_s = 1 / k₁ + 1 / k₂ ⇒ k_s = k₁ k₂ / (k₁ + k₂), T_s = 2π √[ m (k₁ + k₂) / (k₁ k₂) ].
Parallel: k_p = k₁ + k₂, T_p = 2π √[ m / (k₁ + k₂) ].
cards.hint: Opposite to electrical resistors! Springs in series add reciprocally; parallel springs add directly.

cards.q: A spring of constant k is cut into n equal parts: What is the spring constant of each part?
cards.a: k' = n · k.
cards.hint: Because length becomes L/n and k ∝ 1/L. If cut into 2 halves, each half has constant 2k!

cards.q: Composition of two collinear SHMs of same frequency: Resultant Amplitude R and Phase δ?
cards.a:
R = √[ A₁² + A₂² + 2 A₁ A₂ cos(α₁ - α₂) ]
tan δ = [ A₁ sin α₁ + A₂ sin α₂ ] / [ A₁ cos α₁ + A₂ cos α₂ ].
cards.hint: Exactly analogous to the vector addition formula for two vectors of magnitudes A₁, A₂ with angle (α₁ - α₂).

cards.q: Resultant amplitude of two collinear SHMs when phase difference is (1) 0°, (2) 180°, (3) 90°?
cards.a:
1. In phase (Δα = 0): R = A₁ + A₂ (Maximum).
2. Opposite phase (Δα = π): R = |A₁ - A₂| (Minimum; 0 if A₁ = A₂).
3. Quadrature (Δα = π/2): R = √(A₁² + A₂²).
cards.hint: If A₁ = A₂ = A and Δα = 2π/3 (120°), resultant amplitude is R = A.

cards.q: Angular SHM: Restoring torque and time period?
cards.a:
Restoring Torque: τ = - c θ, where c is restoring torque per unit twist.
Differential equation: I (d²θ / dt²) + c θ = 0 ⇒ d²θ / dt² + ω² θ = 0 (where ω = √(c / I)).
Time Period: T = 2π √(I / c).
cards.hint: I is moment of inertia about rotation axis. Example: Torsional pendulum.

cards.q: Period of vibration of a bar magnet of magnetic moment M in uniform magnetic field B?
cards.a: T = 2π √[ I / (M B) ], where I is moment of inertia of magnet.
cards.hint: Restoring torque is τ = - M B sin θ ≈ - (M B) θ for small angular displacements.

cards.q: Damped Oscillations: Equation of motion and amplitude decay formula?
cards.a:
Differential equation: m (d²x / dt²) + b (dx / dt) + k x = 0, where b is damping coefficient.
Amplitude decay: A(t) = A₀ · e^[ - b t / (2 m) ].
cards.hint: Amplitude decays exponentially with time due to viscous/frictional energy dissipation.

cards.q: Angular frequency ω' of Damped Harmonic Oscillator?
cards.hint: Damping strictly REDUCES the oscillation frequency below the natural frequency ω₀.

cards.q: Free, Forced oscillations, and Resonance?
cards.a:
Free: Oscillations with natural frequency without external driving force.
Forced: Oscillations driven by a periodic external force at driving frequency ω_d.
Resonance: Occurs when driving frequency matches natural frequency (ω_d = ω₀), causing amplitude to become MAXIMUM.
cards.hint: Sharpness of resonance depends on damping: low damping gives very sharp resonance peaks.

cards.q: What is the frequency of kinetic energy and potential energy oscillations in SHM?
cards.a:
2 f (twice the frequency of the SHM particle)!
Since K = (1/2)kA² cos²(ωt) = (1/4)kA² [ 1 + cos(2ωt) ], energy completes TWO full cycles for every ONE cycle of displacement.
cards.hint: Top MHT-CET trap! If displacement frequency is 50 Hz, KE oscillates at 100 Hz.

cards.q: Time taken by a particle starting from mean position to reach x = A/2 vs from x = A/2 to x = A?
cards.a:
From x = 0 to x = A/2: t₁ = T / 12 (since sin(ω t₁) = 1/2 ⇒ ω t₁ = π/6 ⇒ t₁ = T/12).
From x = A/2 to x = A: t₂ = T / 6 (since T/4 - T/12 = T/6).
cards.hint: Particle travels faster near the mean position, so it takes HALF the time (T/12) for the first half displacement compared to second half (T/6)!

cards.q: Period of a simple pendulum inside an accelerating lift?
cards.a:
Lift accelerating upward with a: T = 2π √[ L / (g + a) ] (T decreases).
Lift accelerating downward with a: T = 2π √[ L / (g - a) ] (T increases).
Freely falling lift (a = g): T = ∞ (pendulum stops oscillating, weightless).
cards.hint: Effective gravity g_eff = g + a (upward) or g - a (downward).

cards.q: Effective length of pendulum with a spherical bob of radius r and string of length l?
cards.a: L = l + r (measured from point of suspension strictly to the CENTER OF GRAVITY of the bob).
cards.hint: If water drains out of a hollow sphere, CG first moves down (L ↑ ⇒ T ↑) then returns to center (L ↓ ⇒ T ↓).

cards.q: MHT-CET Trap: If amplitude of SHM is doubled, what happens to its Time Period and Total Energy?
cards.a:
Time Period T remains COMPLETELY UNCHANGED (T is independent of amplitude A).
Total Energy E quadruples (E ∝ A², so E' = 4 E).
cards.hint: Do not confuse energy (which scales as A²) with period/frequency (which is independent of A).
